Teenager Charged With Felony Retaliation Against CSPD Officers During Arrest For Public Intoxication

November 10, 2026 Jeanette Muenchow

A teenager turned a misdemeanor into a felony charge Monday night.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:42
Instaread

College Station Police responded to a welfare check in the 1300 block of Augustine Court Monday around 8:30pm. The reporting party said a male was walking down the street, screaming and yelling profanities, and that he wanted to kill himself.

Officers identified the man as 17-year-old Preston Scott Cone. They say they smelled the odor of alcoholic beverages on his breath.

Arrest records also say that Cone was slurring his speech, had a cut and scratches on his left hand and forearm from him tripping and falling earlier in the day, and had a disheveled appearance — his belt was slightly undone, making his pants sag, one shoe untied, and his hair was messy in appearance.

When asked where he would go next, Cone had no direction of travel, even though he stated various times he knew his home address, but did not know how to get there or where he was currently located. He was reportedly knocking on doors and looking into vehicles in attempt to figure out where he was and get directions to his home. Police also reported recent calls of a male matching Cone’s description walking in the traffic lanes on Harvey Mitchell Parkway South.

Cone was charged with Public Intoxication of a Minor, a Class C Misdemeanor. While enroute to jail, Cone allegedly threatened officers, saying he would pistol whip, slap, run over, and kill the two responding officers.

He was additionally charged with Retaliation, a Third Degree Felony, and remains jailed on $15,000 bond.

  • Bryan FD and Bryan Fire Fighters Association Host “Fill the Boot” Campaign Thursday Through Saturday

    The Bryan Fire Department and the Bryan Fire Fighters Association Local 1204 launch the annual MDA “Fill the Boot” Campaign starting Thursday. Look for firefighters around Bryan Thursday through Saturday. Or, to donate online visit https://checkout.square.site/merchant/ML0WQ25P1D144/checkout/DWAPU4DOZEQ7FREZMSFWLZNW or scan the QR code in the story graphic. Since 1954, the International Association of Fire Fighters (IAFF) has united communities to collect critical funds for the Muscular Dystrophy Association (MDA) – one dollar at a time – through the Fill the Boot program. This year, fire fighters from Bryan Fire Department and Bryan Firefighters Association Local 1204 will continue this legacy during MDA’s 75th anniversary, marking 71 years of support from fire fighters nationwide. Dedicated fire fighters from Bryan Fire Department and Bryan Firefighters Association Local 1204 will take to the streets with boots in hand, asking pedestrians, motorists, and shoppers to help transform the lives of children and adults living with muscular dystrophy, ALS, and other related neuromuscular diseases. The Fill the Boot event will take place on November 12th through 14th across the City of Bryan. The historic partnership between MDA and IAFF began in 1954 when IAFF adopted MDA as its charity of choice. Over the past seven decades, fire fighters have raised more than $710 million for MDA, helping fund over $1 billion in research. These contributions have fueled significant advancements in medical research, including the development of more than 32 FDA-approved treatments for neuromuscular disease since 2015. In addition to Fill the Boot, fire fighters volunteer at MDA Summer Camp, providing children with neuromuscular diseases a week of fun and independence. MDA and IAFF also collaborate to raise awareness and provide resources for fire fighters impacted by ALS. Community members are encouraged to visit fire fighters at intersections across the City of Bryan or donate online at the following link to support this vital cause. About the IAFF: The International Association of Fire Fighters represents more than 340,000 professional fire fighters and paramedics who protect 85% of the nation’s population. More than 3,500 affiliates and their members protect communities in every state in the United States and in Canada. To learn more visit IAFF.org and follow the IAFF at Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram. About Muscular Dystrophy Association: Muscular Dystrophy Association (MDA) is the #1 voluntary health organization in the United States for people living with muscular dystrophy, ALS, and related neuromuscular diseases. For over 70 years, MDA has led the way in accelerating research, advancing care, and advocating for the support of our families. MDA’s mission is to empower the people we serve to live longer, more independent lives. To learn more visit mda.org and follow MDA on Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok, and LinkedIn.   • Two People Arrested At College Station HEB For Stealing $700 in Ninja Drink Makers

    Two people were arrested after a theft at a College Station H-E-B Tuesday evening. An officer with CSPD was conducting a traffic stop in the parking lot of the H-E-B at Texas Avenue and Holleman Drive when he was flagged down by a store employee. 40-year-old Shakithia Lanea Council left the store with two Ninja Slushi Frozen Drink Makers, valued at $349.00 each. Council was attempting to leave the parking lot when she was stopped by the officer who could see one of the drink makers in her backseat. H-E-B provided video footage showing the woman leaving the store with the items after failing to pay. Council was charged with Theft Under $2,500 With Two or More Previous Convictions. She has two theft convictions out of McLennan County (2008 and 2018) and a conviction for theft in Brazos County in 2018. She is free on $25,000 bond. It was her 11th booking in the Brazos County Jail. A man who was in the driver’s seat while Council was in the store was also arrested. Officers say the car smelled of marijuana and witnessed 28-year-old Edward Dewayne Johnson exit the vehicle and attempt to walk away. 0.4 grams of marijuana was recovered from inside the vehicle and Johnson was charged with Possession of Marijuana under 2 ounces. He is free on $2,00 bond. It was his 14th booking in the Brazos County Jail. Got a news tip? e-mail us at news@wtaw.com, text us at (979) 695-1620, or reach out on Facebook or Twitter/X.

  • TAMU 150 Speaker Series Featuring Leaders from The Farmer’s Dog, YETI, JOYRIDE, and AEGIS Aerospace

    The next installment of the Texas A&M Sesquicentennial Speaker Series is taking place Friday. Four former Texas A&M students who transformed their industries will take part in the free public panel at 1:30pm on Friday, November 13th, at Rudder Theatre. Mays Business School Dean Nate Sharp and Flippen Leadership Institute Director Stephen Courtright will moderate “Redefining What’s Possible: Aggie Leaders Who Are Revolutionizing Their Industries From the Inside Out,” featuring: Tyler Merrick ’00, founder and CEO, JOYRIDE: His low-sugar candy brand became the No. 1-selling non-chocolate candy at Target in 2025. Stephanie Murphy ’00 ’14, principal owner and CEO, AEGIS Aerospace: Her company Alpha Space built the first woman-owned facility in space, and today AEGIS operates research platforms on the International Space Station, including one built with Texas A&M. Federico Muyshondt ’03, president and COO, The Farmer’s Dog: He helps lead the fresh dog food company that has delivered hundreds of millions of meals to dogs nationwide. Ryan Seiders ’96, co-founder, YETI: He co-founded the outdoor brand with his brother in 2006, turning a better-built cooler into one of the most recognizable names in outdoor gear. From space exploration and outdoor gear to candy and pet food, the conversation explores how bold ideas and bold leadership can reshape an industry and be a force for good. Attendees will also be able to ask their own questions during an audience Q&A. While the event is free, you will need to reserve at ticket through the MSC Box Office.
